column1: # the separate review of the fixes of results 26.5 (lead ruling 26.7 (라)) and its verification, before any boot (2026-11-19).
# One line per finding: id, severity (the review's), real and before_boot (the verification's), the claim and the
# verification's reading shortened in this record's own words, and what results 26.9 does with it.  The full texts of the
# review and of the verification are not copied here; measurements the reviewer made in scratch and removed are not cited
# as evidence (rule: every count from a kept file); the verification re-derived each claim from committed files and kept
# outputs.  The ids have no fix-decl-04 or fix-decl-07; they are the review's own numbers.

column5: the eval step writes each boot's full eval.txt (about 1 MB, one kept dry-run output above 1 MiB) into the repository's record directory, against lead ruling 26.7 (다) (full output under the kept-output directory with a sha256 and a ledger row, only the head and per-branch tail committed); spec 11 item 15 still calls it small; the eval step's one-run refusal checks only that path, so moving the file by hand reopens it and a re-run overwrites eval_run.txt. The verification: real, the impact procedural (no count depends on where the file sits), but it must be settled before boot 1 because run_cycle.sh is a declared row
column6: code: the eval step writes c1cyc_<s>_eval<N>/eval.txt under the work directory (new directory, refused if it exists) and eval_tail.txt into the record directory; the keep step writes the sha256 lists and ledger rows; protocol 14.14 item 1, spec 11.6 item 1; declaration 4

column5: the per-boot space need of declaration 3 (51,810,304 B [I]) is below what kept measurements of the frozen code show (16-branch explain of the boot shape, the eval output not counted), and commands.txt checks the need only before boot 1 of each build. The verification: real with the kept values (explain 48,750,592 B guard dip, eval 1,036,288 B), about 53.8 MB per boot, 23.8 MB more for 12 boots; the floor stays protected by the guard, so the risk is a late step refused part-way through a boot's processing; the finding's own scratch figures are not kept and not cited
column6: text and code: the per-boot need restated from kept files (records/closure-space3-20261119/need.txt), a need for every boot from the boots remaining, the boot step measures and refuses below it, a measured per-boot value from the boots already run replaces the declared one when larger; lines 9-12 of the 26.8 list archived; protocol 14.14 item 4

column5: the frozen eval script cuts every note at 600 characters with no mark, and the F3 'slot clear only (weak ...)' part comes last, so a unit with many excused creates can lose the weak mark. The verification reproduced it on a scratch world (11 id-excused creates and one slot-clear-only create: note exactly 600 characters, 'weak' absent); unlikely in this cycle [I]; reopening the freeze for it alone is not worth it
column6: dated note in results 26.9 for section 27: count the F3 lines whose note is exactly 600 characters in each kept eval.txt and do not report such a pass as strong; the counts-first note and a fixture at the next revision of the eval script

column5: two branches of the expect_discriminate class rule (a rule-(1) row with two alternatives contexts and no sidecar line; a rule-(2)-only row with context lines) and two cause combinations of the found-use link reason (no namespace-entry line; a loss marker together with an unbound site) have no fixture. The verification: the code follows the texts today and the real control rows of this cycle reach none of the four shapes; fixtures would change two frozen files
column6: dated note in results 26.9: the four untested shapes listed for section 27; fixtures at the next freeze

column5: test_run_cycle.sh tests the boot step's commit check only for the declaration, not for run_cycle.sh, and never reaches the 'missing' branch of a count row; results 26.5 row pre-builds-07 reads as if both files were tested. The verification: a mutant without the run_cycle.sh half and with got=0 for a missing directory still passed 11/11; no wrong boot can follow (run_cycle.sh is a sha256 row verified twice; a missing directory gives rc 1 either way)
column6: code: the two cases added to test_run_cycle.sh (a run_cycle.sh with an uncommitted change: no boot; a counted directory removed: missing); dated note under results 26.5

column5: a second boot-step attempt for the same N overwrites verify_at_boot.txt. The verification: real but smaller than claimed (the git check exits before that line; the nested verify's full record survives as the earlier verify.txt kept under a nanosecond name); what is lost is the one-line capture and its stderr
column6: code: the boot step keeps an earlier verify_at_boot.txt under a new name (UTC nanoseconds) before it writes; the same for every log a step rewrites on a legitimate re-run

column5: the count row counts regular files only, while the boot runner tars everything under ws/exe; an added symlink or FIFO would pass verify. The verification reproduced it (a symlink out of the tree and a FIFO: verify clean, tar kept both); both builds have 0 such entries today
column6: code: the count row counts every entry that is not a directory (find ! -type d); the same as fix-decl-11

column5: the gate step's comment in run_cycle.sh still says every named loss marks its needs unknown-loss; since ef6d38f the judge excludes no-build-id and object-table (NONEVENT_LOSS); only a comment, the gate's output does not depend on it
column6: code: the comment corrected in the revised run_cycle.sh; section 27 cites the judge and the declaration header, never the comment

column5: commands.txt says to check free space before boot 1 of each build against the need written in declaration 3, which is the 12-boot total; read literally it stops c1_post_tx after c1_pre_tx's boots (about 750-800 MB left against 1,036 MB), and any other reading needs a number chosen after records exist. Not disclosed
column6: text and code: a need for each boot from the boots remaining in the cycle (protocol 14.14 item 4), checked by the boot step itself against need rows of declaration 4; commands.txt names it

column5: no command enforces the declared need: 'the boot step measures the space again' in declaration 3 means only the space guard's floor + 60,000,000 B; the df check in commands.txt is a comment with no command. The verification: real (the guard completed at a simulated 900,000,000 B), the same pattern as builds-04; the proposed per-build check must use the remaining boots, not the 12-boot figure
column6: code: the boot step measures df -B1 / (kept boot<N>/space_at_boot.txt) and refuses below the need of the boots remaining (rc 1, no boot)

column5: the per-boot need of 51,810,304 B scales an 8-branch x 45-record regression and leaves out the 46/45 factor and the per-boot eval and expect outputs; kept measurements of the boot shape give about 54 MB per boot and a need of about 1,063 MB, so the 'need met' of results 26.8 rests on an understated figure. The verification: real; neither correction alone flips the verdict, together they do
column6: text: the per-boot need restated from kept files with every part named (records/closure-space3-20261119/need.txt); free measured, short; lines 9-12 of the 26.8 list archived by the same method before the boots

column5: control, chain, stop and gate overwrite their outputs when re-run, with no refusal and no copy; gate.txt decides the boot-number rule, so a FAIL can become a PASS with no trace, against rule 3, protocol 2 and the script's own header. The verification reproduced it in a stub tree (a re-run gate turned FAIL into PASS and boot 2 passed the boot-number rule)
column6: code: control, kzt-text, chain, stop and gate refuse an existing output (rc 2); protocol 14.14 item 2; test cases

column5: declaration 3 line 39 cites predictions2.tsv as the source of the expected outcomes, and the 'read only by the expect step and by F1 of the eval step' clause now reads as if it covered predictions3.tsv; no step reads a predictions file. Wording only; the values are the same

column5: neither run_cycle.sh nor commands.txt puts each boot's eval.txt under the kept-output directory with a sha256 and a ledger row (ruling 26.7 (다)); a manual move removes the eval step's second-run protection. The same defect as fix-judge-01 seen from the commands
column6: code: as fix-judge-01 (the eval directory under the work directory, the tail in the record directory, the keep step with ledger rows checked before the ledger is replaced)

column5: nothing pins the declaration's own sha256: a committed edit between boots, followed by a clean verify, passes the boot step. The verification reproduced it; an edit stays findable afterwards from the kept verify heads and git log, so it need not block the boots; a hard pin only in a step that has to make a new declaration anyway
column6: code (folded into declaration 4): the cycle's first boot writes boot/declaration_pin.txt; every later boot step, the explain, eval and summary steps refuse unless the declaration's sha256 equals it; protocol 14.14 item 5

column5: after the boot step's verify nothing checks the files the evaluation steps read (explain, eval, expect, summary run with no re-verify; the expect and summary outputs carry no input sha256), and the eval passes an optional boot<N>/sheet_boot.tsv that no declaration row covers and that would make precision defined against protocol 14.5
column6: code: the explain step verifies the same N again (verify_at_explain.txt) and refuses unless clean; summary verifies again with N = 5 (verify_at_summary.txt); the eval step always passes --sheets-boot none and refuses if a sheet_boot.tsv exists; protocol 14.14 item 6

column6: code: find ! -type d; values 31 and 31 measured now (no entry other than files and directories); protocol 14.14 item 7; a test case with an added symlink

column5: if the boot step stops after creating the boot's work directory but before cFS starts (the guard refusing at start, not root, UDP 1234/1235 busy), that number can never run again, and the only way forward counts a boot that never happened as a failed first boot and spends the one retry. The verification reproduced it with the real guard forced to refuse
column6: text and code: a boot step whose command ends non-zero while the instance directory was never created is 'not booted' (not a boot of protocol 2); its empty work directory is removed and its log kept under a new name; the same N may run again; protocol 14.14 item 3; test case
